evidence.title: HumanLayer docs: How remote daemons work
evidence.locator: Daemon hosts; Containers; Disposable and suspended hosts; Process life cycle; Browser and native app capabilities; Security model (source apps/docs/explanation/remote-daemons.md at release 0.202.0)
evidence.finding: The host can be any cloud VM, workstation or private machine the user selects. Credentials are lost when a container is recreated unless storage is mounted; treat saved session files as credentials. Sessions bind to a host ID in ~/.humanlayer/riptide/host_id; a host without it registers as new. To resume on a new pod persist credentials, host_id and ~/.claude (Codex history is stored by HumanLayer). A waiting session continues after any length of suspend; if the daemon is silent about two minutes while a session runs or waits for tool approval, the session is marked failed. The browser app at app.humanlayer.com works from a machine or phone but lacks workspace management, an embedded terminal and path auto-complete. Daemons give agents the running user's file and network access; stop the daemon to prevent new sessions.

Reviewers comment on synced documents and later agents read the feedback. Task files live in .humanlayer/tasks/<slug>/ and another workstation downloads them when it runs the task. Markdown, text and JSON(L) sync as text artifacts (10 MB limit); images, PDFs and HTML upload through object storage.

evidence.title: HumanLayer docs: How workflow phases fit together
evidence.locator: Research; Design (PRD/TDD); Structure outline; Implementation; Checkpoints (source apps/docs/explanation/workflow-phases.md at 0.202.0)
evidence.finding: Research checks code, tests and named sources and records current behavior. PRD defines problem, success measure and solution; TDD defines system and program design. Each structure-outline phase names one testable result, its files and checks. Later artifacts take priority; current code is the source of truth for current behavior. Checkpoints: design choices stay open until the user answers, a PRD needs approval of the full solution, a TDD needs separate approval of system and program design, outline feedback never starts implementation and normal implementation waits for manual review.

evidence.title: HumanLayer docs: Skills and workflows reference
